summary: Completed comprehensive testing of 'Shift Requirement Rule' feature. All backend API tests pass (12/12). Fixed frontend bug where shift modal appeared for admin users. The rule 'No operation without shift, except admin' is correctly implemented.

bugs_fixed.issue: Shift opening modal appeared for admin users who are exempt from shift requirement
bugs_fixed.root_cause: The useEffect that shows the shift modal did not check if user is admin
bugs_fixed.fix: Added condition `!isAdmin` to prevent modal from showing for admin users

frontend_ui_tests: Admin login - No shift modal appears (admin exempt)
Admin can click 'Nouvelle vente' button without shift
Admin can open sale dialog without shift
Caissier login - Shift modal appears (non-admin requires shift)
Caissier with shift - Buttons are enabled

api_endpoints_with_shift_requirement.POST /api/sales: require_open_shift dependency - non-admin blocked, admin exempt
api_endpoints_with_shift_requirement.POST /api/stock/losses: require_open_shift dependency - non-admin blocked, admin exempt
api_endpoints_with_shift_requirement.POST /api/supplies: require_open_shift dependency - non-admin blocked, admin exempt
api_endpoints_with_shift_requirement.POST /api/debts/payment/bulk: require_open_shift dependency - non-admin blocked, admin exempt
api_endpoints_with_shift_requirement.POST /api/returns: require_open_shift dependency - non-admin blocked, admin exempt

frontend_hooks.useCanOperate: Returns canOperate=true for admin regardless of shift status

role_based_behavior.admin: Exempt from shift requirement - can perform all operations without shift

critical_code_review_comments: The require_open_shift dependency in auth.py correctly exempts admin users (line 117)
The useCanOperate hook in useShifts.js correctly returns canOperate=true for admin (line 165-170)
All operation buttons use disabled={!canOperate} pattern consistently
